title: Construction 16: Circumcentre and circumcircle of a triangle (straight edge and compass)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with its three perpendicular bisectors meeting at the circumcentre and the circumcircle, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the circumcentre and circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 7$ cm, $|BC| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Use a compass and straight edge and show your construction lines.
example.final: O\text{ is where the perpendicular bisectors meet; circle with centre }O\text{ through }A,B,C

steps.say: Draw the longest side first, then find the third corner with two arcs.

rows.aside: From $A$, draw an arc of radius $5$ cm. From $B$, draw an arc of radius $6$ cm. Label the crossing $C$ and join up the triangle.

steps.say: The circumcentre is the same distance from $A$ and $B$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

rows.aside: Open the compass past half of $|AB|$. Draw an arc above and below $[AB]$ from $A$, then from $B$ with the same width.
Join the two crossings with the straight edge.

steps.say: It is also the same distance from $A$ and $C$, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of $[AC]$.

rows.aside: The two bisectors cross. Label that point $O$.

steps.say: $O$ is the same distance from all three corners.

rows.aside: Put the compass point on $O$ and the pencil on $A$.
Draw the circle. It passes through $A$, $B$ and $C$. Leave all arcs showing.

title: Construct √2 and √3 geometrically
show: right triangle with legs 1 and √2 giving hypotenuse √3, built on a unit segment

example.question: Starting with a segment of length 1 unit, construct a segment of length $\sqrt{3}$ units. Show by calculation that its length is $\sqrt{3}$.

steps.say: Draw a line and mark $A$ and $B$ with $|AB| = 1$. Construct a perpendicular to $[AB]$ at $B$ (Construction 4). Mark $C$ on it with $|BC| = 1$.

rows.aside: Use the compass to copy the unit length each time.

steps.say: Join $A$ to $C$. By Pythagoras, the square of $|AC|$ is the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
Construct a perpendicular to $[AC]$ at $C$. Mark $D$ on it with $|CD| = 1$. Join $A$ to $D$.

rows.aside: The two sides of the new triangle are $|AC| = \sqrt{2}$ and $|CD| = 1$.

steps.say: Apply Pythagoras to the new triangle.

title: Find the area between a curve and the x-axis
show: parabola y=x²-5x+4 with the area between it and the x-axis from x=1 to x=4 shaded below the axis

example.question: Find the area enclosed between the curve $y = x^2 - 5x + 4$ and the $x$-axis.

steps.say: The area is enclosed between the points where $y = 0$. Set the function equal to $0$ and factorise.
Integrate between the roots $\hl{1}{1}$ and $\hl{1}{4}$.
Top limit first, then subtract the bottom limit.
The curve is below the $x$-axis between the roots, so the integral is negative. An area cannot be negative, so take the positive value.

title: Find the area between two curves
show: parabola y=4x-x² and line y=x crossing at x=0 and x=3 with the enclosed region shaded

example.question: The curves $y = 4x - x^2$ and $y = x$ cross at two points. Find the area enclosed between them.

steps.say: The limits are where the curves meet. Set the two $y$ values equal and solve for $x$.

rows.aside: So $x = \hl{1}{0}$ or $x = \hl{1}{3}$. These are the limits.

steps.say: Test one $x$ between the limits. The curve with the bigger $y$ is the top curve.

rows.aside: The curve is on top, so the integrand is curve minus line.

steps.say: Subtract bottom from top to get one function. Integrate it from $\hl{1}{0}$ to $\hl{1}{3}$.
Put in the upper limit, then take away the value at the lower limit.

title: List outcomes and apply the fundamental principle of counting
show: tree or list showing soup choices branching into sandwiches then drinks

example.question:
A cafe lunch deal is one soup, one sandwich and one drink. There are 2 soups, 5 sandwiches and 3 drinks.
(a) How many different deals are there?
(b) The cafe adds one new item to one group. Which group gives the most deals?
example.final: (a) $30$ deals  (b) add a soup, giving $45$ deals

steps.say: Each stage can be chosen in any way, whatever was picked before. So multiply the number of choices at each stage.
Add one to one group at a time and multiply again.
The biggest total wins. State the answer in words.

rows.aside: $\hl{2}{45}$ is the largest, so the cafe should add a **soup**.

title: Construct a sample space for two independent events
show: table/grid of outcomes: H and T against spinner 1 to 4

example.question:
A fair coin is tossed and a fair spinner numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 is spun.
(a) List all the possible outcomes.
(b) Find the probability of a head and an even number.

steps.say: Pair each coin result with each spinner number. Do one row at a time so none are missed.
Look for a head and an even number: the pairs $(H,2)$ and $(H,4)$.
Divide the wanted outcomes by all outcomes.
